The AI Marketing page now has a Claude strategy button. It sends this period's totals and the trade area around the club to Claude, and in a minute or two you get facts, strategies, local niches and a 30, 60 and 90 day plan. It writes in Korean or English, whichever the page is set to.

The last 30 days had 1,016 rounds. Weekend mornings are the busiest: public golfers at 10.7 rounds a day and GolfNow at 8.2. Weekday afternoons after noon are nearly empty. Members cluster on weekday mornings, and so far zero percent of rounds are linked to a customer record.

Strategy one: fill weekday afternoons. Offer a weekday after-noon rate with its own promo code to Welland and Pelham neighbours and Niagara College students. Text only people who agreed to texts, and hold back ten percent of the list as a comparison group. Measure rounds in that slot and code uses.

Strategy two: move weekend mornings from GolfNow to direct booking. About forty percent of weekend morning golfers come through GolfNow. Invite them to sign up on the website at check-in, and give a cart or snack bar perk for booking direct. The goal is a lower GolfNow share on weekend mornings.

Strategy three: the Hamilton boundary. Stoney Creek, Binbrook and Mount Hope are thirty-five to forty-five minutes away and growing fast with young families. They need a reason to drive past closer courses, so offer weekend twilight rates bundled with a Niagara wine country day trip. Grimsby and West Lincoln sit on the way.

By area, the biggest markets are St. Catharines at about 137,000 people and Hamilton at about 570,000. The closest are Welland at about 56,000 and Pelham at about 18,000. Tourism shift workers in Niagara Falls have weekdays off, which makes them good weekday afternoon golfers. Populations are approximate, from the 2021 Census.
